messages:
maya: Nightly vuln scan flagged a few Go deps with CVEs. Can we triage and decide pin/patch/backport plan?

maya: Summary from vuln-bot:
- CVE-2026-1002 (google.golang.org/grpc) - deserialization crash, remote exploit possible
- CVE-2026-1105 (github.com/golang-jwt/jwt) - signature verification edge-case
- CVE-2026-2100 (Go stdlib net/http) - request smuggling header parsing fix (requires runtime upgrade)

maya: Affected services: inference-runtime, routing, auth-proxy. Dedicated customers with on-prem may need guidance.

ben: Thanks. Do we have exploitability details?

oliver: grpc CVE has PoC in the wild (limited). jwt vuln needs specific token shape, but we use jwt for internal service-to-service tokens so high risk. net/http is only exploitable with crafted upstream proxies; lower immediate risk but still important.

ben: Ok. Proposed priority: 1) grpc 2) jwt 3) net/http (runtime). Also check oauth2 client libs (golang.org/x/oauth2) for related token leakage.

sri: Agreed. For remediation approach:
- grpc: bump to v1.60.2 which contains fix, run golden-path canary on staging traffic for 48h, then rollout to production with 5% -> 25% -> 100%.
- jwt: bump to github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.4.1, add targeted unit tests for signature edge-cases, add runtime fuzz test.
- net/http: needs Go runtime upgrade to go1.22.x which includes header parsing fix. We'll coordinate with infra for runtime bump; treat as medium priority and schedule with minor release window.

ben: Sample go.mod changes I was going to include in the PR:
```
require (
    google.golang.org/grpc v1.60.2
    github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.4.1
)
```
Add a go.sum sync and `go test ./...` in CI.

maya: For Dedicated/private customers: we should provide a short KB describing the risk and mitigation steps (pinning vs runtime upgrade). Also check KMS client libs — we use `cloudkms` wrapper in auth-proxy, confirm no dependency impact.

oliver: I'll scan our KMS wrappers. If we need a key rotation or re-encrypt step, we should call out in the KB.

ben: I'll open an RFC PR with the pinned versions + canary job and smoke tests. Assigning myself.

sri: I'll update the vuln triage playbook: add scoring for customer-facing tokens (score +2), require audit log entry for any dependency CVE changes. Also add a note to ensure all changes create an audit event in Console (model: dependency.update).

maya: Who can own backporting guidance for older branches? We still run release-1.4 for a few enterprise installs.

oliver: I can coordinate backports for release-1.4. Likely we pin grpc and jwt patches and document that net/http requires an OS/runtime upgrade — we can't backport that easily.

ben: PR CREATED: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/2345 - includes pins + unit tests + canary job. Marked WIP.

vuln-bot: Automated scan linked CVE-2026-1002 -> PR #2345 referenced.

security-bot: Created ticket SEC-4592: "grpc/jwt/nethttp triage + patch rollout". Owners: ben (PR), oliver (backports), sri (playbook), maya (KB). ETA: staging canary start within 24h.

maya: Great. Next steps:
- ben: finish PR and request review from eng-runtime and eng-ml
- oliver: KMS wrapper scan + backports mapping
- sri: update playbook and add audit-entry checklist
- security-bot: add follow-up reminder in 72h

maya: Thanks all. Ping here when canary starts. :thumbsup:
